title: Weaver project configuration
description: What a project declares to Weaver: its rules, the checks that observe them, and what the engine cannot guess about it.

exclude.description: Folders no check and no review looks at, relative to the repository root.

finish.description: When a unit of work is finished, and how long the checks may hold the agent.

headings.description: The headings of the final message that declares the work finished. Without them, every end of turn does.

skill.description: The file that tells the agent how to write the final message, relative to the repository root. Weaver guards it, and names it to an agent that stops with changed files and without the headings.

maxRounds.description: How many times in a row the checks may refuse the end of a turn. After that the agent may stop, its unit of work still open.

deadlineSeconds.description: How long one run of all the checks may take.

concurrency.description: How many checks run at once.

review.description: What a reviewer judges: the independent review of a unit of work against the rules written here. An agent that did not write the change judges it once the checks pass, and the agent that wrote it answers each finding, fixed or not fixed with a reason. A finding never holds the change by itself. The owner has four words for a request: `#no-review` asks for no review of that work, `#review` takes it back and has a review that failed tried again, `#critical` asks for the runtime that did not write the change, `#simple` for the one that did.

runtime.description: Who reviews: a runtime by its name, `same` for the one that wrote the change, `other` for the one that did not.

reviewers.description: The model and the effort of each runtime when it reviews. Without them, the runtime chooses.

critical.description: Where a mistake costs the most: such a change is reviewed by the runtime that did not write it, whatever `runtime` says.

paths.description: A change that touches one of these paths, as globs relative to the repository root.

lines.description: A change that adds or modifies more lines than this.

experiments.description: Whether the reviewer may run commands and write files to show what it suspects. It then works in a copy of the working tree, outside the repository and removed after the review; what else it may reach, such as a running stack, is for the skill to say. Without this, it only reads.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one review may take. A review that does not answer in time holds nobody: the owner is told that the rules were not judged, and `#review` in a later request has it tried again.

waitSeconds.description: How long the end of a turn waits for a review. A review that runs longer goes on by itself: the unit of work stays open, and the next end of turn gives its findings.

maxRounds.description: How many reviews may send the agent back to work, for one request. What a later review finds waits for the owner.

skill.description: The file that tells the reviewer how this project wants its changes reviewed, relative to the repository root. Weaver guards it.

rules.description: The rules the reviewer judges. Each key is the name of a rule, as the agent and the owner read it: `external-data-parsed` says more than a code.

issue.description: The command that files an issue when the owner closes a point as `issue` with `weaver close`, with `{title}` and `{body}` where they go. Without it, closing as `issue` only records it.

scripts.description: The project's own scripts, which Weaver cannot guess whether they write files. Each entry is a command and its first words, such as `npm run api:types`. What is declared here wins over what Weaver guesses.

writers.description: Scripts that write files, such as a generator: everything that changes while one runs is the agent's work, and is checked.

readers.description: Scripts that only read, such as a check of the project's own: what changes while one runs is never the agent's work.

checks.description: What a program judges at the end of a task: the project's own programs, run on the diff of a unit of work, each with the rules it stands behind. Each key is the name of a check.

guards.description: What is refused before a tool runs, each with the sentence that says why. Each key is the name of a guard.

verify.description: The command that judges, with its arguments. An argument `{files}` becomes the changed files the check is about.

fix.description: A command that repairs what it can before `verify` judges what is left: a formatter, a linter's autofix. It runs on the unit's own files, and what it rewrites stays the agent's work.

cwd.description: Where the command runs, relative to the repository root.

when.description: The changed paths that make the check run, as globs. Without it, any change does.

reads.description: How the verdict is read. `exit`: from the exit status. `findings`: from the last line printed, `{"findings": [...]}`, where each finding gives the name of a `rule`, a `file`, a `message` and optionally a `line`.

after.description: The check that must be done before this one starts, for a check that reads another's output.

rules.description: The rules this check stands behind. Each key is the name of a rule, as the agent and the owner read it: `no-any` says more than a code. A check with no rule of its own lists places for a rule of the review that names it as its `candidates`.

statement.description: The rule the guard holds, as it is told to the agent it refuses.

writes.description: Paths the agent may not write, create, move or remove, as globs relative to the repository root. Only what a call names is refused before it runs: a script that writes one of them is not seen.

runs.description: Commands the agent may not run. Each entry is a command and words that appear in that order among its arguments: `git commit` also refuses `git -C api commit`.

checkRule.description: A rule a check stands behind: the sentence told to whoever broke it, or an object when the rule says more.

statement.description: What the rule says, as it is told to whoever broke it.

level.description: Who a failure is for. `gate`: the agent, which is held until it is fixed. `human`: the owner, who reads it in the report; the agent is not held.

reviewRule.description: A rule the reviewer judges: the sentence it is given, or an object when the rule says more.

statement.description: What the rule says, as it is given to the reviewer and told to whoever broke it.

scope.description: Where the rule applies, as globs. Without it, everywhere.

evidence.description: For a rule about what the code does, such as a defect: a finding must carry the experiment that shows it. Without one it is a suspicion, which the owner reads and the agent does not.

candidates.description: The check that lists the places this rule is about, for the reviewer to judge one by one. That check reads `findings`.

model.description: The model the runtime reviews with.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks, in the words of its runtime (`low`, `high`, ...).

maxTurns.description: How many turns one review may take. Claude Code holds a review to it; Codex has no such limit.

maxCostUsd.description: How much one review may cost, in dollars. Claude Code holds a review to it; Codex has no such limit.
